decisions.decision: Which rulings does this plan inherit from plans 1 to 3?
decisions.ruling: Keep the html/ namespace (the user's virajp.dev config overrides html/attrs-newline and html/use-baseline). Credit the MIT code in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md plus a one-line source header in each ported file, test files included. Put the code in src/plugins/html/. Dependencies follow the user's criterion: a direct dependency is not a concern; port what brings peer ranges or conflicting transitive trees. No Vue support. Each edit unit runs mise x -- mise run code:format --fix before it returns. Each test file connects RuleTester to vitest itself (RuleTester.describe, it, itOnly from vitest) and imports from src/.
decisions.rejected: A new namespace; a separate package

decisions.decision: Which packages are kept and which are ported?
decisions.ruling: Port @html-eslint/eslint-plugin 0.68.0 (peer eslint >=8.0.0||^10.0.0-0; pins @eslint/plugin-kit ^0.4.1 against our 0.7.3). Keep @html-eslint/parser, @html-eslint/core, @html-eslint/template-parser and @rviscomi/capo.js as direct, exact-pinned, bundled dependencies: none has a peer, and their transitive trees (css-tree, html-standard, vscode-css-languageservice) are not shared with another direct dependency. @html-eslint/types, es-html-parser and @types/estree become exact-pinned devDependencies, for type-only imports. The ported language uses our @eslint/plugin-kit 0.7.3 (a direct dependency since plan 2); adapt it to the 0.7 API where the tests show a difference.
decisions.rejected: Port the parser and core; keep the plugin

decisions.decision: How is the JavaScript source ported?
decisions.ruling: Convert to strict TypeScript, as in plans 1 to 3. The JSDoc types become TypeScript types; upstream lib/types/*.ts and lib/languages/types.ts are ported as they are. Behavior stays the same.
decisions.rejected: Vendor the JS with allowJs and checkJs

decisions.decision: Which html rules do we port?
decisions.ruling: 65 rules of @html-eslint/eslint-plugin 0.68.0: all except the deprecated no-extra-spacing-attrs. The 18 rules that the preset enables are among them.

decisions.decision: Do we port the support for HTML inside JS template literals?
decisions.ruling: Yes. Port lib/rules/utils/template-literal.js and the template branches of the rules, and the template test cases (the upstream createRuleTester("espree") testers).

At tag v0.68.0 of yeonjuan/html-eslint, under packages/eslint-plugin/: tests/rules/<rule>.test.js for each of the 65 rules (inline RuleTester cases, both testers); tests/rule-tester.js to tests/unit/plugins/html/helpers/rule-tester.ts, which takes the plugin object as a parameter; tests/rules/utils/template-literal.test.js (U1); tests/languages/*.test.js (U1; a case that needs a rule goes to U6); tests/inline-disable.test.js (U6, in language mode). Not ported: tests/e2e/, tests/configs.test.js and tests/plugin/export.test.js (D11 a; no configs; the export shape differs).
decisions.rejected: Golden snapshots only; port every test

decisions.decision: Where does the rule configuration live, and how is parity proved?
decisions.ruling: In the html preset. The plugin index (U6) exports meta, rules (merged from rules/group-a.ts to group-d.ts) and languages { html }; no configs. The preset reproduces html.configs.recommended exactly (its rule severities and options) and keeps its own three rule overrides (html/indent [error, 2], html/no-extra-spacing-tags {enforceBeforeSelfClose: true}, html/require-closing-tags {selfClosing: always}), files ["**/*.html"] and language html/html. After U6, the golden snapshots do not change at all; any golden change stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: configs in the plugin; accept golden changes

decisions.ruling: One review unit after U6, because the change ships runnable code. Execution mode teams, because wave 2 has four edit units; if a team cannot start, the run uses solo.
MINOR: the deprecated rule html/no-extra-spacing-attrs is removed; a scan of ~/Projects on 2026-11-22 found no consumer config that names it.

decisions.decision: Round 1 rulings review: version list, html-standard, version drift, the indent folder, the gates commit
decisions.ruling: (a) U6 owns src/cli/commands/version.ts and removes the ^@html-eslint/ pattern, because --version lists plugins only (plan 2 D13 e). (b) U6 adds html-standard 0.0.13 as a direct, exact-pinned, bundled dependency: no-redundant-role imports it, and it has no peers. (c) Version drift of the kept packages is accepted: they are exact-pinned, and an upgrade happens only through p:upgrade, whose tests and golden snapshots catch a break; no hold is added. (d) Upstream indent is a folder (lib/rules/indent/{index,indent,indent-level}.js): U2 owns src/plugins/html/rules/indent/ with the same three files, and each header names its own upstream path. (e) U9 only verifies: when no file changes, it makes no commit.
decisions.rejected: Accept the new --version lines; rely on hoisting for html-standard; hold the kept packages; merge indent into one file; an empty commit

decisions.decision: Round 2 rulings review: e2e, parser mode, the template-literal util test, entities.json, the RuleTester wiring
decisions.ruling: (a) The upstream e2e test (tests/e2e/) is not ported: it turns on the deprecated no-extra-spacing-attrs and uses the @html-eslint/ prefix; the rule tests and the golden snapshots cover the same ground. (b) tests/inline-disable.test.js is ported in language mode: plugin key html, language html/html, and html/ in the rule names and the eslint-disable comments. The parser-mode code paths in the rules stay as upstream has them; no test uses parser mode. (c) U1 ports tests/rules/utils/template-literal.test.js to tests/unit/plugins/html/utils/template-literal.test.ts. (d) lib/data/entities.json becomes src/plugins/html/data/entities.ts, a module whose default export is the same object; a script generates it from the upstream JSON (never retyped), so tsc builds it into dist/ with no tsconfig change; its first line is the source header. (e) The shared helper tests/unit/plugins/html/helpers/rule-tester.ts connects RuleTester to vitest for every HTML test, the one exception to D1. (f) The TEST_ESLINT_LEGACY_CONFIG branch and the parserOptions remap of upstream rule-tester.js are dropped.
decisions.rejected: Port e2e with edits; keep parser mode in tests; import JSON with resolveJsonModule; wire RuleTester in each file

decisions.decision: Round 3 rulings review: the parserOptions remap, capo.d.ts, espree, the empty with-rules file, U1 verification
decisions.ruling: (a) The helper keeps the parserOptions remap of upstream rule-tester.js (it lifts languageOptions.parserOptions, for example templateEngineSyntax, to languageOptions); only the TEST_ESLINT_LEGACY_CONFIG branch is dropped. This amends D11 f. (b) @rviscomi/capo.js 2.3.1 ships its own types: the port drops upstream lib/rules/utils/capo.d.ts. (c) U6 adds espree as an exact-pinned devDependency, at the version in node_modules/espree/package.json (the one ESLint installs), because the template-literal test imports it directly. (d) U6 creates tests/unit/plugins/html/language/with-rules.test.ts only if U1 left out at least one case. (e) The U1 verification also runs tests/unit/plugins/html/utils.
decisions.rejected: Drop the remap and edit the test data; keep capo.d.ts; rely on hoisting for espree; an empty test file

decisions.decision: What does a unit do when a ported upstream test fails only because ESLint 10 or vitest is stricter? (ruled by the user on 2026-11-22 for all B08 plans)
decisions.ruling: A ported upstream test case that fails only because ESLint 10's RuleTester or the vitest wiring is stricter than upstream's setup (jest on ESLint 9) — not because the rule behaves differently — may have its test setup changed: for example, remove a duplicate case, or add a property that ESLint 10 requires. Never change the expected messages, message ids, locations, output or suggestions. List each change as DECIDED; the review unit checks them. A case whose expected result differs stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: Stop and ask for each case; apply it to one plan only

decisions.decision: How are eslint-disable comments for unknown rules and strict-TypeScript errors in ported code handled?
decisions.ruling: (a) A ported file may drop an eslint-disable or eslint-enable comment that names a rule this repo does not define, or rewrite it to the rule of this repo that it means; ESLint 10 reports an unknown rule in such a comment as an error, so code:lint would fail. (b) Where the repo's strict TypeScript (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, .js import extensions) rejects ported code, a unit fixes it only with changes that have no runtime effect: non-null assertions, casts, type annotations, import type, and .js or /index.js on relative imports. No runtime guard is added. List each kind of change as DECIDED. (Ruled for all B08 plans on 2026-11-22, from the rulings review of plan 6.)
decisions.rejected: Define the unknown rules; add runtime guards
